newsitem.title: CANADA: Two Manitoba towns evacuated as Red River surges.
newsitem.headline: Two Manitoba towns evacuated as Red River surges.

text.p: More than 1,200 Manitoba residents were ordered to flee their homes on Tuesday as the Red River surged into the southern part of the province and a young boy became the first known Canadian to die in the flood.
Police said four-year-old Kevin Michael Maendel of the New Rosedale Hutterite Colony near Portage-la-Prairie drowned in a culvert along the Assiniboine River, which drains into the Red.

The town of Emerson, on the Canada-North Dakota border evacuated 750 residents, while 400 people abandoned their homes in Dominion City, 10 miles (16.09 km) north of the border, Manitoba Emergency Management Organization executive coordinator Harold Clayton said. Emerson's hospital was evacuated on Monday.
The customs station at Emerson was closed at midnight on Monday ahead of Friday's forecast flood crest and 65 Canadian soldiers helped reinforce ring dikes there.
Meanwhile, 83 other people sought refuge behind ring dikes around St. Pierre Jolys as Red River tributaries overflowed, engulfing their homes, Clayton said.

"We're ready for the last record (flood) we had, but not for anything above that. We'll just have to do the best we can," said Morris Rural Municipality Reeve Herm Martens, the local equivalent of the mayor in Morris, 30 miles (48.28 km) south of Winnipeg..
Martens issued a voluntary evacuation order to more than 200 people in the district about 30 miles (48.28 km) north of the U.S. border.

Floods in 1950 and 1979 left 400 square miles (1,036 sq km) of land between the U.S. border and Winnipeg under water. This year's crest may well cover double that area and take weeks to drain, emergency officials said.

"We haven't had a flood like this since the 1860s, so we're not sure how long the water will take to drain or when these people can return home," Manitoba Natural Resouces flood liaison engineer Larry Whitney said.

Whitney said that While southern communities were at high risk, a massive crecent-shaped ditch around Winnipeg should be able to handle the flood. An estimate of the expected flood level was revised upward last Friday to 2 to 3 three feet above the worst flood Manitoba has seen so far this century, Whitney said.

The C$63.2 million ($45.2 million) Red River Floodway was completed in 1968 after a 1950 flood forced 100,000 Winnipeggers to evacuate the city. More than 630,000 people live in the Manitoba capital now.
Highway 75 from the U.S. border to Winnipeg was closed just south of the city late on Monday as other roads were washed out.
States of emergency were declared in the rural municipalities of Franklin, Morris, Tache and Montcalm as well as the towns of Dominion City, Ste. Anne and Emerson.
